name: Avatar
usage: Avatars of conversations, teams and projects; `leading` of list items; account menus; online status

props.name: name
props.description:
Person's or item's name: the first character is shown, and the whole name determines the tone in a stable
way (the same name has the same color everywhere).

props.name: size
props.description: Size in pixels: commonly 20 (tables, tags), 28 (sidebars) or 32 (lists).

props.name: ring
props.description: Accent ring, for avatars that need to stand out, such as teams or the current user.

props.name: icon
props.description:
Shows an icon instead of text (such as system notifications), on a neutral fill without a tone: a name, or an
icon component such as Lucide's `Bell`.

props.name: status
props.description: Status badge at the bottom right (a StatusDot tone), such as online status; not shown when omitted.

props.name: statusLabel
props.description: Accessible name of the status badge, such as "Online"; the default name of the tone is used when omitted.

types.name: IconName
types.summary:
Name of a registered icon. Only the icons listed here can be used; they are Lucide icons under shorter names
(`trash` is Lucide's `Trash2`, `more` is `Ellipsis`). All names at runtime: `iconNames`. Props that take an
icon also accept an icon component instead of a name (see IconComponent).

types.name: IconComponent
types.summary:
An icon component, such as Lucide's `Plus` (`import { Plus } from 'lucide-react'`), accepted wherever an icon name
is: `<Button icon={Plus}>`, `<Icon icon={Plus} />`, menu items and so on. Names (`icon="plus"`) are convenient
and work in data such as menu configurations, but cover only the registered icons (`iconNames`); a component can
be any Lucide icon, or an SVG of your own. Both are drawn with the same size, stroke width and `tone`.

fields.name: tone
fields.description:
Tone: `success` for normal, `warning` for attention, `danger` for errors, `neutral` for inactive, `accent` for
reminders. The caller maps business meanings (online, running, disabled, and so on) to tones and describes
them with `aria-label`.

types.name: IconComponentProps
types.summary:
Props that Icon passes to an icon component. Lucide icons (`import { Plus } from 'lucide-react'`) accept them; a
component of another icon set, or an SVG of your own, works too if it accepts them, or passes them on to its
`<svg>`.

fields.name: strokeWidth
fields.description:
Stroke width in the units of a 24 × 24 view box, already scaled for `size`: the line is 1.75 px wide on screen
by default, whatever the size.

fields.name: color
fields.description:
Stroke color: `currentColor` (the text color) or a semantic color variable, such as
`var(--vl-color-danger)`.

fields.name: aria-hidden
fields.description: `true` for a decorative icon (hidden from screen readers).

fields.name: aria-label
fields.description: Accessible name of a meaningful icon.

types.name: BaseProps
types.summary:
Accessibility and test props shared by all layout primitives (and, partly, by other components): `testId`,
`aria-label`, `role` and `id`, rendered on the root element.

examples.name: Basic
examples.title: Basic usage
examples.description:
Shows the first character of the name and picks one of five tones from the name, so the same name has the same
color everywhere. Common sizes are 20, 28 and 32.

examples.name: RingAndIcon
examples.title: Ring and icon
examples.description:
`ring` adds an accent ring for avatars that should stand out, such as teams or the current user; `icon` shows an
icon instead of text (for example, system notifications) on a neutral fill.

examples.name: WithStatus
examples.title: Status badge
examples.description: `status` takes a tone of StatusDot and appears at the bottom right; `statusLabel` is its accessible name.
